title: The Undergrowth That Speaks in Colors

features.name: abandoned shopfront
features.desc-on-touch: A storefront buried in the undergrowth, its paint faded to spectral colors—reds and blues speaking to each other through the leaves. Windows show inventory that was never sold: bottles, bolts, dreams in boxes. The wild has moved in through the door.

features.name: color conversation
features.desc-on-touch: Where moss and rust have learned to speak to each other in hues the archive has no names for. The undergrowth translates: green-dark saying something to orange-earth, and both responding in frequencies that have nothing to do with sound.

features.name: shed roof visible
features.desc-on-touch: A corrugated roof breaking through the ferns, still speaking in the colors it was painted: a red that has learned patience, a blue that has learned to belong to the forest. The archive keeps its buildings as leaves.

features.name: overgrown sign
features.desc-on-touch: A painted direction-post, fern-wrapped and fading. The letters have learned colors they didn't have before—rust-reds, moss-greens. It points everywhere and nowhere, and the undergrowth has accepted both answers at once.

inscription: where the wild has learned to paint its own arguments

file.name: Chromatic_Layers_Undergrowth_Study.txt
file.note: Field notes on how the forest processes color. Built things fade into the spectrum, and the undergrowth learns to read what the colors are still saying about their first lives.
